guidance.summary: Petrobras reported record Q3 output of 3.512M boe/d, which beat consensus and ran above the implied 2026 plan. The company made no formal guidance change and has not yet released Q3 financial results.

evidence.claim: Q3 oil and gas output was a record 3.512M boe/d, up 11.7% year on year and 5.3% quarter on quarter.
Output beat the Visible Alpha consensus of 3.48M boe/d, and Brazil oil output of 2.83M bpd exceeded the peak forecast in the 2026-2030 business plan.
Ativa analyst Ilan Arbetman said the quarter's output is above Petrobras' implied 2026 guidance.

guidance.label: Guidance changes

analyst_actions.summary: Analyst actions tilted positive. BofA raised its target to $28 from $22, Weiss upgraded the stock and Goldman kept its Buy rating, while Wall Street Zen trimmed its rating to buy from strong-buy.

evidence.claim: BofA raised its price target on PBR to $28 from $22.
Goldman Sachs keeps USD 24.30 target for Petrobras stock.
Wall Street Zen downgraded PBR to buy from strong-buy.
Weiss Ratings upgraded PBR to buy (b) from buy (b-).

analyst_actions.label: Analyst actions

litigation_regulation.summary: ANP postponed the hearing on its forced gas-sale program to Nov 19, so that risk remains unresolved. Petrobras' new exploration blocks and an inflow of about US$859M from reservoir balancing agreements are routine, and no new fines or lawsuits surfaced.

evidence.claim: ANP postponed the Gas Release Program hearing from Oct 21 to Nov 19.
Petrobras signed the Berbigão and Sururu balancing agreements with Shell, TotalEnergies and Petrogal and will receive a net of about US$859 million.
Petrobras acquired the Azurita and Cruzeiro do Sul blocks with 100% stakes.

litigation_regulation.label: Litigation and regulation

customer_concentration.summary: China took 40% of Q3 oil purchases while exports hit a record. There were no major customer wins or losses.

evidence.claim: China took 40% of Petrobras' oil purchases in Q3, and exports of oil and derivatives hit a record 1.25M bpd.

customer_concentration.label: Customer concentration

insider_activity.summary: Petrobras is a foreign private issuer and files no Form 4s, and no insider transactions were reported.
insider_activity.label: Insider activity

product_competitive.summary: The news was mixed. A long-term Cheniere LNG deal and higher fuel sales are positives, but diesel is priced well below import parity, which raises the risk that Petrobras breaks its pricing policy.

evidence.claim: Petrobras signed a 22-year LNG purchase agreement with Cheniere for 0.8 Mtpa.
Abicom put Petrobras' refinery diesel about R$3.53/l below import cost as the federal import subsidy lapsed, and Itaú BBA warned large gaps could push Petrobras to break its pricing policy.
Q3 domestic fuel sales rose 6.4% quarter on quarter to 1.854M bpd, led by diesel.

product_competitive.label: Product and competitive news

writeup.headline: Petrobras rates Hold at 59: strong growth and momentum offset by negative free cash flow and debt.
writeup.thesis: Petrobras scores 59, a Hold, six points short of the Buy band. Growth is the standout at 94, with TTM revenue growth of 30.2% and growth sped up by 51.1 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores just 39 and the balance sheet only 19. A 53.1% gross margin and 16.0% operating margin are offset by an FCF margin of -11.0%, and cash covers only 0.48 of debt, with net debt carried alongside negative free cash flow. Trend scores 67: shares are up 82.9% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and the price is 15.7% above its 200-day average, but the stock is 6.0 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and 15.8% below its 52-week high. News scores 60, helped by record Q3 output and mostly positive analyst actions, and valuation could not be scored.
key_risks: Negative free cash flow (FCF margin of -11.0%) while carrying net debt, with cash covering only 0.48 of debt
Diesel priced well below import parity raises the risk of a break from its pricing policy and political interference
ANP's forced gas-sale program hearing, postponed to Nov 19, remains unresolved
Heavy reliance on China, which took 40% of Q3 oil purchases, plus exposure to oil price swings
Shares 6.0 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and 15.8% below their 52-week high
what_would_change: Up to Buy (6 points away): a return to positive free cash flow would lift both the quality and balance sheet scores
Up: Q3 financial results that confirm the record output and keep revenue growth strong, or further analyst upgrades
Down to Sell (15 points away): a sharp slowdown in revenue growth combined with a weakening trend score
Down: an adverse ANP gas-sale ruling, or a pricing-policy break that hurts margins and turns news risk negative
